title: Ribbon runs: Positive proof strip
summary: String runs. Keep the positive numbers.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`line` is text. A character is one letter, digit, space, or punctuation mark.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `runLengths`. A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", `runLengths` is [2, 1, 2].
2. Create a list `positiveValues` that keeps only the numbers in `runLengths` that are greater than 0, in the same order.
3. Complete `ribbonRunsPositiveProofStrip` so it returns `positiveValues`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `line` is "rg  zci", then `runLengths` is [1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1] and `ribbonRunsPositiveProofStrip` returns [1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1].

Rules
- Keep repeated numbers.
- If `runLengths` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `line` is "illrx mrrri".
TEST DATA 2: `line` is "LL lLL".

referenceSolutions.python:
def ribbonRunsPositiveProofStrip(line):
    a=line
    out=[]
    i=0
    while i<len(a):
        j=i+1
        while j<len(a) and a[j]==a[i]: j+=1
        out.append(j-i)
        i=j
    return [x for x in out if x>0]
